goal: Adds wallet support for sending to silent-payment addresses, the counterpart to the receiving side
Lets users send privacy-preserving payments without the recipient revealing a reusable address
reviewability: Needs rebase, marked stale and dirty by the mergeable-state bot
Review #35301 first since this PR is stacked on it and conflicts with 13 other open PRs
agreement: Concept ACK with no objections raised (rkrux)
Multiple rounds of style and test-hardening nits, all addressed by the author (theStack, rkrux)
No standing objections remain, feedback has been iterative and resolved

categories.name: rpc
why: P3 because it adds a new RPC built mainly to support this PR's own test suite
No clear external consumer beyond internal testing, keeping impact modest

categories.name: tests
why: P4 because most of the added test volume actually pins wallet-specific behavior, not framework coverage
Only the fuzz-util additions for new destination variants count here, and those are incremental

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because it creates a shared cryptographic primitive intended for RPC, wallet, and future node consumers
Correctness here determines whether silent-payment outputs are computed correctly everywhere downstream
Errors would propagate into fund-affecting wallet logic

categories.name: wallet
why: P2 because it delivers the wallet half of a widely anticipated privacy feature
Touches fund-flow-sensitive paths like coin selection and RBF recomputation where mistakes could misdirect funds
Prerequisite for the broader silent payments project to be usable end to end
